VIDEO.title: Jesus Hid a Message in Plain Sight At the Last Supper
VIDEO.series: The Gospel of Matthew Every Word (playlist of 58 videos)

kicker: Study aid · Matthew 26:17-29 · Episode 51 (#54 of 58 in the playlist)
hand: As it is written of Him
SUMMARY: The teacher reads Matthew 26:17-29. On the first day of Unleavened Bread Jesus sends the disciples to a certain man: 'My time is near; I am keeping the Passover at your house.' At the table He says one of them will betray Him: 'He who dipped his hand with Me in the bowl.' Judas asks, 'Surely not I, Rabbi?' Then Jesus takes bread ('this is My body') and a cup ('this is My blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many for forgiveness of sins') and says He will not drink of the fruit of the vine until He drinks it new in His Father's kingdom.
The account is also in Mark 14, Luke 22 and John 13. 'My time' is the appointed time God gives (Ecclesiastes 3:1; Genesis 1:14). Jesus appears to go to His death willingly, at Passover.

The Passover meal followed an order (seder) built around four cups of wine, with blessings over the wine and bread, the son's question ('Why is this night different?'), the story of the exodus, the lamb, unleavened bread and bitter herbs, and the Hallel psalms (113-118). Jesus explains the bread and cup as His body and the blood of a new covenant.

The roots run deep: the betrayer who ate my bread (Psalm 41:9); the Servant crushed by Yahweh's will (Isaiah 53:10); 'the blood of the covenant' (Exodus 24:8; Zechariah 9:11); the new covenant (Jeremiah 31:31-33); the Servant given 'as a covenant to the people' (Isaiah 42:6). The four cups may answer the four promises of Exodus 6:6-7; some think Jesus waits to drink the fourth.

The lesson: as the Son of Man devoted His whole life to living out the entirety of God's word, so the disciples of the Son of Man must also do the same. 'The Son of Man is going, just as it is written of Him' (26:24).
QUOTES: As the son of man devoted his whole life to living out the entirety of God's word, so the disciples of the son of man must also do the same.
Jesus explains these elements as they relate to his body and blood of a new covenant.
The disciples are meant to see with their eyes, their physical eyes, but understand through the lens of Tanakh.
They must live out the totality of God's word in every aspect of life.

left.text: And He said, “Go into the city to a certain man, and say to him, ‘The Teacher says, “My time is near; I am keeping the Passover at your house with My disciples.”’”

right.text: There is an appointed time for everything. And there is a time for every matter under heaven—

lines.text: How did Jesus know His time had come? We're not told: perhaps divine foreknowledge, perhaps He knew what Judas was planning. He appears to go willingly to die at Passover.
The video reads Genesis 1 as a chiasm centered on 1:14, where the lights are 'for signs and for seasons'; the word means appointed times (mo'adim).

src.text: Now when evening came, Jesus was reclining at the table with the twelve disciples. And as they were eating, He said, “Truly I say to you that one of you will betray Me.”

lines.text: The meal was organized around four cups of wine. Families reclined, a sign of freedom; the father blessed the wine, the son asked why this night is different, and the father retold the exodus, from disgrace to glory (Deuteronomy 26:5-11).
The Mishnah: 'the distributors of charity should not give a poor person less than four cups of wine' and the son asks, 'Why is this night different from all other nights?' (Mishnah Pesachim 10:1, 4).
The blessings: over wine, 'Who creates fruit of the vine'; over bread, 'Who brings forth bread from the earth' (Mishnah Berakhot 6:1).

left.text: And He answered and said, “He who dipped his hand with Me in the bowl is the one who will betray Me.

right.text: Even my close friend in whom I trusted, / Who ate my bread, / Has lifted up his heel against me.

lines.text: The meal probably began with a morsel of bread dipped in a bowl of sauce (haroset); this may be the morsel Judas dipped before leaving (John 13:26-30).
'The Son of Man is going, just as it is written of Him' (26:24): perhaps Isaiah 53 or the anointed one cut off in Daniel 9:26.

src.text: Now while they were eating, Jesus took some bread, and after a blessing, He broke it. And giving it to the disciples, He said, “Take, eat; this is My body.”

lines.text: The father explained the lamb, the bread and the bitter herbs by the exodus. Jesus explains the elements by His body and blood. The bread is unleavened (Exodus 12:15; Deuteronomy 16:3).
The video mentions a custom of hiding a wrapped piece of the broken bread for the children to find, which some scholars link to the Messiah; it says it is unclear whether this happened in Jesus' day.

left.text: So Moses took the blood and sprinkled it on the people and said, “Behold the blood of the covenant, which Yahweh has cut with you in accordance with all these words.”

right.text: As for you also, because of the blood of your covenant, / I have set your prisoners free from the waterless pit.

lines.text: Zechariah 9 joins the king on a donkey (9:9) to the blood of the covenant and freed prisoners, as Jesus spoke of the least of these in prison.
Jeremiah 31:31-33 promises a new covenant written on the heart, and in Isaiah 42:6 and 49:8 the Servant is given 'as a covenant to the people.'

COVENANT.title: As it is written of Him

src.text: But Yahweh was pleased / To crush Him, putting Him to grief; / If You would place His soul as a guilt offering, / He will see His seed, / He will prolong His days, / And the good pleasure of Yahweh will succeed in His hand.

lines.text: The Lord is behind the whole thing, in keeping with Jesus' 'appointed time' and His prayer in 26:39. Jesus becomes the lamb for a new Passover.

src.text: Say, therefore, to the sons of Israel, ‘I am Yahweh, and I will bring you out from under the hard labors of the Egyptians, and I will deliver you from their slavery. I will also redeem you with an outstretched arm and with great judgments. Then I will take you for My people, and I will be your God; and you shall know that I am Yahweh your God, who brought you out from under the hard labors of the Egyptians.

lines.text: Why four cups? Four promises: I will bring you out, deliver you, redeem you, and take you for My people. The fourth is the cup of consummation.

left.text: I shall lift up the cup of salvation / And call upon the name of Yahweh.

right.text: And after singing a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.

lines.text: Psalms 113-118 (the Hallel) were sung through the meal. The video invites us to imagine Jesus singing 'Precious in the sight of Yahweh is the death of His holy ones' (116:15).
The Mishnah: 'they pour him the fourth cup. He completes hallel over it' (Mishnah Pesachim 10:7).

src.text: But I say to you, I will not drink of this fruit of the vine from now on until that day when I drink it new with you in My Father’s kingdom.”

lines.text: Some conclude that Jesus did not drink the fourth cup and left the meal unfinished, and that 'let this cup pass from Me' (26:39) refers to that fourth cup, filled by His blood on the cross. Others disagree; the video offers it to chew on.

BACKGROUND.p: Lambs were slaughtered at the temple on the afternoon of 14 Nisan and eaten that night inside Jerusalem; the seven-day Feast of Unleavened Bread followed (Exodus 12; Deuteronomy 16).

Mishnah Pesachim 10, written down about AD 200, describes the four cups, the questions, the explanation of lamb, matza and bitter herbs, and the Hallel. How much was already practiced in Jesus' day is debated.
Banquets were eaten reclining on couches, leaning on the left arm; the Mishnah says even the poorest should recline at Passover, 'as free and wealthy people recline' (Mishnah Pesachim 10:1).

DEBATES.p: Matthew, Mark and Luke present it as the Passover; John's timeline places the crucifixion on the day of Preparation (John 19:14). Scholars harmonize this in several ways.
The video reports the view that Jesus left the fourth cup undrunk; others think Luke's two cups (Luke 22:17, 20) or the Mishnah's order cannot be pressed that far.
Christian traditions differ on how Christ is present in the Lord's Supper: as real presence, spiritual presence, or memorial.

CAREFUL_INTRO: Small slips worth knowing (offered gently; the video's main points stand):
CAREFUL: Judas went to the chief priests (26:14), not the Pharisees.
The usual name 'Great Hallel' belongs to Psalm 136, not Psalm 118 (Talmud Pesachim 118a).
The custom of hiding a piece of matza for children to find (the afikoman) is attested only much later; the video rightly says it is unclear for Jesus' day.
The line 'The world has yet to see what God can do with a man fully consecrated to him' is usually traced to Henry Varley, who said it to D. L. Moody.

QUESTIONS: What does 'My time is near' show about how Jesus faced His death?
How does knowing the Passover order help you read the Last Supper?
Why do you think each disciple asked, 'Surely not I, Lord?'
What do Exodus 24, Zechariah 9 and Jeremiah 31 add to 'the blood of the covenant'?
Where are you living out God's word, and where only knowing it?
How might your life be 'a letter of Christ' (2 Corinthians 3:3) this week?
APPLICATION_VIDEO: The lesson: as the Son of Man devoted His whole life to living out the entirety of God's word, so the disciples of the Son of Man must also do the same. The video does not set aside the new covenant, atonement or resurrection; it adds that those trained to be like their rabbi (Luke 6:40) are invited to live out God's word in every aspect of life, like 'a letter of Christ... written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God' (2 Corinthians 3:3).
APPLICATION_ADDED: Study note (added): before you next take the Lord's Supper, read Exodus 12 and Jeremiah 31:31-34, and name one command of Jesus you will put into practice that week.

## Summary (from the video)
- The teacher reads Matthew 26:17-29. On the first day of Unleavened Bread Jesus sends the disciples to a certain man: 'My time is near; I am keeping the Passover at your house.' At the table He says one of them will betray Him: 'He who dipped his hand with Me in the bowl.' Judas asks, 'Surely not I, Rabbi?' Then Jesus takes bread ('this is My body') and a cup ('this is My blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many for forgiveness of sins') and says He will not drink of the fruit of the vine until He drinks it new in His Father's kingdom.
- The account is also in Mark 14, Luke 22 and John 13. 'My time' is the appointed time God gives (Ecclesiastes 3:1; Genesis 1:14). Jesus appears to go to His death willingly, at Passover.
- The Passover meal followed an order (seder) built around four cups of wine, with blessings over the wine and bread, the son's question ('Why is this night different?'), the story of the exodus, the lamb, unleavened bread and bitter herbs, and the Hallel psalms (113-118). Jesus explains the bread and cup as His body and the blood of a new covenant.
- The roots run deep: the betrayer who ate my bread (Psalm 41:9); the Servant crushed by Yahweh's will (Isaiah 53:10); 'the blood of the covenant' (Exodus 24:8; Zechariah 9:11); the new covenant (Jeremiah 31:31-33); the Servant given 'as a covenant to the people' (Isaiah 42:6). The four cups may answer the four promises of Exodus 6:6-7; some think Jesus waits to drink the fourth.
- The lesson: as the Son of Man devoted His whole life to living out the entirety of God's word, so the disciples of the Son of Man must also do the same. 'The Son of Man is going, just as it is written of Him' (26:24).

### Read the meal through its order
Learn the order of the Passover meal (the seder), then ask where Jesus' words fit into it and how He changes their meaning.

## Key people
- The certain man: Host of the Passover, unnamed in Matthew. [Background] Mark and Luke add a man carrying a water jar and a large upper room (Mark 14:13-15).
- The twelve: Each asks, 'Surely not I, Lord?' [Background] Only Judas calls Him 'Rabbi' (26:25).
- Judas Iscariot: The one who dipped his hand in the bowl. [Background] 'You yourself said it' (26:25).
- Moses: Sprinkled the blood of the covenant at Sinai. [Background] Exodus 24:3-8 ratifies the covenant after the people answer, 'All the words... we will do.'

## Places [Background]
- Upper room (traditional) (named in the video): Where Jesus kept the Passover; traditionally placed on Mount Zion.
- Temple: Passover lambs were slaughtered in its courts on 14 Nisan.
- Mount of Olives (named in the video): After singing a hymn, they went out here (26:30).

## Key terms
- Seder: 'Order': the set order of the Passover meal.
- Four cups: The four cups of wine of the Passover meal (Mishnah Pesachim 10).
- Hallel: Psalms 113-118, sung at Passover.
- Haroset: A sauce or paste for dipping at the Passover meal.
- Tanakh: The Hebrew Bible: Torah, Prophets and Writings.
- Halakha: 'Walking': living out the Torah in daily life.

## Historical and cultural background [Background: established]
- Passover and Unleavened Bread: Lambs were slaughtered at the temple on the afternoon of 14 Nisan and eaten that night inside Jerusalem; the seven-day Feast of Unleavened Bread followed (Exodus 12; Deuteronomy 16).
- The Mishnah's Passover: Mishnah Pesachim 10, written down about AD 200, describes the four cups, the questions, the explanation of lamb, matza and bitter herbs, and the Hallel. How much was already practiced in Jesus' day is debated.
- Reclining: Banquets were eaten reclining on couches, leaning on the left arm; the Mishnah says even the poorest should recline at Passover, 'as free and wealthy people recline' (Mishnah Pesachim 10:1).

## Early witnesses [Background: sourced]
- John Chrysostom (c. AD 390): "For if the type was a deliverance from such bondage, how much more will the truth set free the world, and will He be delivered up for the benefit of our race." Homilies on Matthew 82, on 26:26-28. NPNF 1.10 (public domain).
- John Chrysostom (c. AD 390): "He gave thanks, and sang an hymn after the giving, that we also may do this selfsame thing." Homilies on Matthew 82, on 26:30. NPNF 1.10 (public domain).

## Where scholars differ [Background: debated]
- Was it a Passover meal? Matthew, Mark and Luke present it as the Passover; John's timeline places the crucifixion on the day of Preparation (John 19:14). Scholars harmonize this in several ways.
- The fourth cup The video reports the view that Jesus left the fourth cup undrunk; others think Luke's two cups (Luke 22:17, 20) or the Mishnah's order cannot be pressed that far.
- 'This is My body' Christian traditions differ on how Christ is present in the Lord's Supper: as real presence, spiritual presence, or memorial.

## Careful reading notes
Small slips worth knowing (offered gently; the video's main points stand):
- Judas went to the chief priests (26:14), not the Pharisees.
- The usual name 'Great Hallel' belongs to Psalm 136, not Psalm 118 (Talmud Pesachim 118a).
- The custom of hiding a piece of matza for children to find (the afikoman) is attested only much later; the video rightly says it is unclear for Jesus' day.
- The line 'The world has yet to see what God can do with a man fully consecrated to him' is usually traced to Henry Varley, who said it to D. L. Moody.

## Reflection and discussion questions
1. What does 'My time is near' show about how Jesus faced His death?
2. How does knowing the Passover order help you read the Last Supper?
3. Why do you think each disciple asked, 'Surely not I, Lord?'
4. What do Exodus 24, Zechariah 9 and Jeremiah 31 add to 'the blood of the covenant'?
5. Where are you living out God's word, and where only knowing it?
6. How might your life be 'a letter of Christ' (2 Corinthians 3:3) this week?

## Application
- (video) The lesson: as the Son of Man devoted His whole life to living out the entirety of God's word, so the disciples of the Son of Man must also do the same. The video does not set aside the new covenant, atonement or resurrection; it adds that those trained to be like their rabbi (Luke 6:40) are invited to live out God's word in every aspect of life, like 'a letter of Christ... written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God' (2 Corinthians 3:3).
- Study note (added): before you next take the Lord's Supper, read Exodus 12 and Jeremiah 31:31-34, and name one command of Jesus you will put into practice that week.
